title: marketGapDirection averages ordinal ranks across source pools of 169-903 rows; 55.4% of offense rows and 95.8% of pick rows carry the OPPOSITE label under pool normalization, and Calvin Ridley renders BUY on /rankings because of it
claimUnderTest: marketGapDirection/Magnitude 'quantify the disagreement between retail and expert consensus' and drive the /rankings EDGE column plus the trade page's BUY/SELL signal.
observed: _compute_market_gap takes the arithmetic mean of retail ranks and of consensus ranks and subtracts them — raw ordinals, no pool normalization. The same module's _percentile_rank_spread docstring states this is invalid: 'an effective spread of 100 doesn't mean the sources disagree, it means one is on a 1-185 scale and the other is on a 1-600 scale.' Live pool sizes: dlfIdp 169, dlfSf 278, ktcSfTep 499, idpTradeCalc 903. Recomputing the same comparison in percentile space (rawRank/poolSize, exactly what the sibling function uses) flips the direction on 214 of 386 offense rows (55.4%) and 23 of 24 pick rows (95.8%). Confirmed in the live DOM: Calvin Ridley renders EDGE = BUY on http://127.0.0.1:3000/rankings. Separately, all 293 ranked IDP rows carry direction 'none' because KTC publishes no defenders, so the EDGE column is permanently blank for 40% of the board (honestly, but the column has no coverage note). frontend/lib/display-helpers.js::marketEdge recomputes the identical ordinal-mean logic client-side, so the frontend mirrors rather than checks the backend.

numericProof.formula: ordinal: diff = consensusMean - retailMean = 269.769 - 325 = -55.23 -> consensus_premium (BUY). percentile: 0.6616 - 0.6513 = +0.0103 -> retail_premium (the opposite).

userImpact: A manager opens /rankings, sees Calvin Ridley flagged BUY ("experts value him above retail — buy low from a retail-first partner"), and offers for a player the retail market actually prices ABOVE the expert consensus. The same field drives getPlayerEdge on /trade, the buy/sell advanced filter and the EdgeRail. No caveat is shown.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed independently on the live stack with a new worked example (Calvin Ridley) and live DOM proof of the rendered BUY badge. My rates: offense 55.4% (prior 47%), picks 95.8% (prior 97%).

whatWorks: marketGapDirection/Magnitude reproduce exactly from effectiveSourceRanks — 0 mismatches over 740 ranked rows. The arithmetic is right; the inputs are incommensurable.
rootCause: _compute_market_gap predates the percentile-normalisation work that fixed the same class of bug in _percentile_rank_spread, and was never revisited when the source registry grew from 3 similar-depth boards to 21 boards spanning 169-903 rows.
requiredRepair: Normalise both sides by each source's own pool size before differencing (reuse the pool-size map _percentile_rank_spread already builds), re-express marketGapMagnitude in percentile points, and re-derive MARKET_GAP_MIN_DIFF / MIN_EDGE_RANK_GAP for the new units. Update frontend/lib/display-helpers.js::marketEdge in lockstep or delete it in favour of the backend stamp.
dependencies: Blocks any re-tuning of MARKET_GAP_MIN_DIFF; touches the same effectiveSourceRanks map as W03-F004.
